name: AI access
summary: Let Claude or another AI tool read and act here through MCP, as one person, with that person’s rights.

rebuild.builds: AI access, as a feature a workspace can switch off. An admin makes a personal MCP token for someone (shown once, only its hash kept) and anyone revokes their own; an AI tool using the token acts as that person through the MCP server, with that person's rights, every change logged as theirs “via MCP”. The tokens are listed on their own Workspace section, AI access (/workspace/ai, admins), in Settings (your own) and on a person's page (Make an MCP token). Off, the server refuses every token of the workspace with one sentence, but still lists its tools; no token can be made; Workspace, Settings and People show no tokens; /workspace/ai says it is switched off. Tokens are kept, not revoked: switching it back on makes them work again. An admin switches it on Workspace, Features, after a read-back that names the tokens.
entry: The core keeps a workspace's switched-off modules (Workspace.modulesOff) and refuses a switched-off module's actions (stage 2).
The MCP server answers JSON-RPC over HTTP with a bearer token, loading the token's workspace and its modulesOff for every request (the AI tools' stage).
exit: Switched off, every MCP request but initialize and tools/list is answered with “AI access is switched off in {workspace}. An admin can switch it on in Faro, under Workspace, Features.”, tools/list still lists the tools, and the token's lastUsedAt does not move.
Switched off, making a token is refused with “AI access is off in {workspace}.”, and revoking one still works.

Switched off, Workspace has no AI access section (/workspace/ai is Page not found with “AI access is switched off in {workspace}. An admin can switch it on in Workspace, Features.”), Settings has no “Your MCP tokens” and a person's page has no Make an MCP token (journey U175).

Switching off first reads back, from the rule aiAccessReadBack, the tokens that stop working (the first five by person and name, then how many more) and the changes AI tools made here; switching back on, only when tokens were kept, names those that work again. With no token it acts at once.
set_feature switching AI access off answers “AI access is off in {workspace}. This connection stops working now. An admin switches it back on in Faro.”
gaps: AI access is a switch, not yet a folder of its own (SW7 moves it): its screens (src/ui/AiAssistants.tsx; the AI access section in src/screens/Workspace.tsx; the tokens in src/screens/Settings.tsx and src/screens/People.tsx), its rules (src/domain/actions.ts createToken and revokeToken; the read-back in src/domain/switchOff.ts) and its table (okr_api_tokens, migration 0010) are still the core's, and so is the door in server/mcp.ts. This folder holds its section, its Help article and its AI tools; src/app/reads.ts aiAccessOn is the one place that asks whether it is on.

A token is not yet declared as the module's record (AS part 2's records extension point is SW7's, with a field the store transforms for its secret), so a build without the module still loads and saves tokens as the core's; its server stays open, answering the core’s tools, and only the token tools are missing.
No conformance rows: the demo workspace has no tokens (they work only in the real app), so there is nothing to count.
